name: Vlissingen
title: Vlissingen Ultrasonic Thickness Measurement for Ships
description: Ultrasonic thickness measurement in Vlissingen and Zeeland: pre-docking and in-dock hull structure gauging, ESP renewal survey support and piping checks.
h1: Ultrasonic Thickness Measurement and Hull Inspection in Vlissingen
intro: Vlissingen sits where the Westerschelde meets the North Sea, so much of the traffic bound for Antwerp, Ghent and Terneuzen passes its waterfront, and Damen Shiprepair Vlissingen docks ferries, offshore vessels, dredgers and cargo ships at Vlissingen-Oost. Superintendents use us for thickness gauging in Vlissingen before and during those dockings, and for condition readings on ships at the Sloe area berths. Each job is staffed by a team mobilised from India and sent to the vessel in Zeeland.

highlights.p: Damen Shiprepair Vlissingen takes ferries, offshore vessels, dredgers and short-sea cargo ships into dock. In-dock gauging to the TM plan runs alongside the yard's steel programme and the class surveyor's close-up survey.
Deep-draught ships bound upriver often wait for pilots and tidal windows off Vlissingen. A planned wait can carry deck, piping and void-space readings if launch access and the sea state allow.

Chemical and product tankers at the Vlissingen-Oost jetties and fruit carriers at the cold-store terminals offer short, defined windows for piping, deck and hold or tank gauging under each terminal's rules.

p: Vlissingen is one of the three port areas of North Sea Port, the cross-border port authority formed when Zeeland Seaports and the Port of Ghent merged, alongside Terneuzen and Ghent. The town's own waterfront holds the Damen naval shipbuilding yard, the pedestrian ferry to Breskens and the base of the Scheldt pilots, while the industrial port at Vlissingen-Oost, around the Sloe, handles chemicals, oil products, fruit, dry bulk and project cargo. Offshore wind farms off the Zeeland coast bring installation and support vessels into the port as well. There is no large container terminal at Vlissingen, so its own callers are mainly industrial, reefer and project ships.

Much of the traffic that passes Vlissingen is not calling there. Ships bound for Antwerp, Ghent and Terneuzen change pilots off the town, and deep-draught vessels time their passage of the Westerschelde to the tide, waiting in the estuary or further offshore when the window is missed. For those vessels Vlissingen is a convenient place to put people on board, but the work has to fit a short, weather-dependent window. Ships that do call at Vlissingen-Oost tend to stay for the length of their cargo operation, and ships entering the repair yard stay for the full docking.

That gives the port an unusual inspection profile. Docking work dominates: Damen Shiprepair Vlissingen handles a broad mix of ferries, offshore and dredging vessels and short-sea cargo ships, and their superintendents want pre-docking estimates and in-dock gauging that keeps the steel programme inside the planned days. Ferry and ro-ro operators in particular need car-deck, ramp and stern-door structure gauged while the vessel is out of service, because their timetable leaves no other time. Around that sits a smaller stream of condition gauging on tankers and reefers at the Sloe berths, and occasional readings on ships waiting for the Scheldt.

facilities.h: Where the work is done: Vlissingen-Oost, the Sloe and the estuary
p: Damen Shiprepair Vlissingen at Vlissingen-Oost is the main docking facility, and in-dock gauging there follows the class TM plan and the surveyor's close-up programme. The team works from the yard's staging and lighting, records readings against frame and strake references, and marks plates that need renewal so the yard can schedule its steel crew without waiting for a second round of measurements. Where the superintendent wants an estimate first, we gauge the ship on an earlier call, or on arrival before she enters the dock.

Away from the yard, the industrial jetties in the Sloe area handle chemical and product tankers, dry bulk carriers and project cargo ships, and the cold-store quays receive fruit carriers and refrigerated cargo ships. Each terminal sets its own permit rules. Terneuzen, across the estuary, has its own jetties for the chemical industry there, and the same team can cover both in one mobilisation. Gauging on ships waiting for the Westerschelde is possible by launch, but it should be planned as a defined, limited scope — deck, accessible voids and machinery-space piping — rather than a full programme, because the window closes when the tide turns.
list: Damen Shiprepair Vlissingen, Vlissingen-Oost — pre-docking and in-dock gauging for renewal and intermediate surveys on ferries, offshore vessels, dredgers and cargo ships.
Sloe area chemical and oil jetties — deck, manifold and piping checks on tankers during cargo operations; tank gauging only when the ship is gas-free.
Cold-store and fruit terminals at Vlissingen-Oost — hatch, hold and deck structure readings on refrigerated cargo ships after discharge.
Dry bulk and project cargo quays — hold, hatch coaming and tank-top gauging on bulk carriers and heavy-lift ships once the holds are clear.
Westerschelde anchorages and waiting areas — limited-scope condition gauging by launch on ships waiting for pilots or a tidal window.
Terneuzen jetties across the estuary — piping and deck-structure gauging on chemical tankers, combined with Vlissingen work in one mobilisation.

context.h: Rules and market forces for ship inspection in Zeeland
p: Vlissingen is a Dutch port, so Paris MoU port state control applies, and the Westerschelde and its approaches are part of the North Sea SOx ECA, which limits fuel sulphur to 0.10%. For scrubber-fitted ships, the river passage to Antwerp or Ghent is where wash-water rules matter most: local restrictions on open-loop discharge can apply in the estuary and in port, so check the current position with the agent before switching the system on. Wash-water and overboard lines on these ships are worth gauging at every docking.

The market here is shaped by the cross-border port and by offshore energy. North Sea Port draws chemical, steel and agribulk traffic to both countries, and the wind farms off the Zeeland and Belgian coasts keep installation, cable-lay and crew-transfer vessels moving through Vlissingen. Dredging is constant on the estuary, which is maintained to keep the deep-water route to Antwerp open, so dredgers are among the vessels working here year-round. Older ships on these routes face the same EU ETS and FuelEU Maritime pressures as anywhere in Europe, and owners want measured steel data before committing to another survey cycle.

jobs.p: UTM in Vlissingen splits between dockings at Vlissingen-Oost and shorter jobs on trading ships. For dockings the TM plan and survey status set the scope; for trading ships the scope is set by what the berth, the cargo operation or the tide allows. Either way the superintendent receives readings mapped to the ship's structure, ready to use at the survey or the next yard stay. The examples below show the range.
list: A ro-pax ferry docking at Damen Shiprepair Vlissingen for its renewal survey: shell, car-deck and ramp-structure gauging to the TM plan, with crack detection at known fatigue details.
A trailing suction hopper dredger in dock: gauging of hopper structure, suction pipe and pump-room piping, where abrasive wear concentrates, ahead of steel renewal.
A chemical tanker at a Sloe area jetty: cargo and ballast piping wall-thickness checks under the terminal permit, with cargo tanks gauged at a later gas-free stop.
An offshore wind support vessel between campaigns: deck, crane pedestal and tank gauging alongside at Vlissingen-Oost, before the charterer's condition survey.
A bulk carrier waiting off Vlissingen for an Antwerp tidal window: deck and accessible void gauging by launch, timed to the expected wait.

logistics: The nearest large international airports are Amsterdam Schiphol and Brussels, each a road or rail journey from Zeeland; Rotterdam The Hague Airport is closer for some European connections. The ship's agent arranges ISPS gate passes for the yard or terminal, and launches for any work in the estuary. Vlissingen work by a team from India depends on Schengen visas being in hand, so docking dates should reach us early. Changes to tidal windows can move a waiting ship's schedule, and we plan with the agent's latest estimate.

faqs.q: Can you gauge a ship while it waits off Vlissingen for an Antwerp tidal window?
faqs.a: Sometimes, for a small, defined scope. Transfer is by launch arranged through the agent, the sea state off the estuary decides whether people can board, and the ship may weigh anchor as soon as its window opens. Deck plating, accessible voids and machinery-space piping fit; tank and hold programmes do not. For anything larger, plan the work for the berth or the yard.

faqs.q: Can you gauge a vessel while she is docked at Damen Shiprepair Vlissingen?
faqs.a: Yes, when the owner or manager engages us and the yard admits the team under its site rules. Access, permits and staging are coordinated with the yard through the superintendent. Readings follow the ship's TM plan and are reported so that the yard can plan renewals and the class surveyor can review the data during the survey.

faqs.q: Can one mobilisation cover Vlissingen and Terneuzen or Ghent?
faqs.a: Yes. The three port areas of North Sea Port are close together, and a team in Zeeland can move between a docking in Vlissingen and a tanker in Terneuzen or a bulk carrier in Ghent. Tell us the ships and dates together and we will sequence the work, keeping each vessel's gas-free and access constraints in mind.

faqs.q: What does a dredger docking in Vlissingen typically need gauged?
faqs.a: Wear concentrates where spoil moves: hopper plating and bottom doors, suction and discharge pipework, dredge pump connections and the structure around the draghead gantries. Those areas are gauged on a denser grid than the TM plan's minimum, alongside the normal hull programme, so the superintendent can see wear rates and plan renewals before the next dredging campaign.
